echoedStructuralKeys.comment: The app's serializer echoes structural values back into the long-format parameters object: plugin-base.js getSerializableParameters() re-emits the assigned channel and bus indexes under their short names, Brickwall Limiter adds its class name under pluginType, and both Horn Resonators duplicate the node's enabled switch under en. All of them are dropped unconditionally; the node keeps being the source of truth. Modal Resonator's en is a genuinely independent processing switch and must keep being folded into enabled. Expected parameters are asserted key by key, not exhaustively.

expected.reason: the echoed en is a duplicate of the node switch, so enabled stays true
Modal Resonator's en is an independent processing switch and still disables the effect

bareArrayPipeline.comment: The app still loads a preset file whose top level is a bare array of long-format entries as the pipeline (js/electron/presetIntegration.js and js/app.js), so files in that shape exist in the wild and both bindings accept them. A bare array of short-format entries keeps the existing guidance; the first entry that is an object decides.

bundledPresetCorpus.comment: The app's bundled presets/**.effetune_preset corpus. Both bindings import the same files; the listed ones describe more than one audio path and are rejected in both languages.

appSerializerCorpus.comment: Every plugin in the app's plugins.txt, exported by the app's own long-format serializer (js/utils/serialization-utils.js getSerializablePluginStateLong) in its default state, plus a channel='R' variant for the twelve plugins whose export echoes structural keys back into parameters. Both bindings import each node and must reach the annotated outcome. Regenerate by re-running the app serializer; do not hand-edit the nodes.

outcomeLegend.imports: the node imports and yields the listed effect types, each on the listed channel
outcomeLegend.flattened: the node is a Section: it is folded into the surrounding chain and contributes no effect
outcomeLegend.assetBackedRejected: the semantic effect replaces the app's filter-design parameters with a precomputed impulse-response asset, so the app export carries no convertible parameters; both bindings reject the node up front with the listed error type and message rather than reporting the app's parameters as unsupported fields
